claim.why_it_matters: Two index entries merged on one line. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered PDF page 935 (printed page 911, index) shows at the top of the right column two separate index entries on separate lines: 'Equivalent arithmetic expression  634' and 'ERASE clause  322'. The markdown (page-935.md line 53) has them as one paragraph line, 'Equivalent arithmetic expression 634 ERASE clause 322', with no line break between them, while every neighbouring entry ends with a '\' hard break. The entry boundary is lost, so a reader or parser sees one headword 'Equivalent arithmetic expression 634 ERASE clause' with page 322. No text is missing and both page numbers are present in order, so this is a structural defect in the informative index only, with no normative effect. The claim quotes both sources accurately.
